assets.title: The Flood Tablet (Epic of Gilgamesh, tablet XI)
assets.creator: Unknown scribe; Neo-Assyrian culture. Photograph by Fæ, 15 July 2010.
assets.depictedPeriod: Ancient Mesopotamian literary narrative; not Jonah
assets.provenance: Excavated by Hormuzd Rassam at Kouyunjik, Nineveh, per British Museum record.
assets.rightsVerifiedBy: Codex; exact Commons file record and history inspected 2026-10-25
assets.rightsStatement: Independent photograph by Fæ, licensed CC BY-SA 3.0. WebP conversion by BibleMap, full frame retained; derivative under the same license. No British Museum photograph reproduced.
assets.requiredAttribution: The Flood Tablet, British Museum K.3375. Photo: Fæ / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0; converted to WebP.
assets.altText: Broken clay tablet on a modern mount, covered with rows of wedge-shaped cuneiform marks in two columns.
assets.historicalFit: Excavated evidence of literary culture in seventh-century BCE Nineveh. Does not date or verify Jonah’s visit, or establish literary dependence.
assets.editorialReason: Makes writing and the preservation of stories visible within the city’s history.

assets.title: Jonah Under the Gourd Vine
assets.creator: Unknown sculptor; Anatolia, late Roman–early Christian
assets.depictedPeriod: Later Christian reception of Jonah 4; not an ancient Assyrian scene
assets.provenance: John L. Severance Fund, 1965.239. Exact ancient findspot is not established in the inspected record; no findspot or original use inferred.
assets.rightsVerifiedBy: Codex; exact object Public Domain statement and CMA Open Access policy inspected 2026-10-25
assets.rightsStatement: Object record explicitly permits copying, modification and distribution; CMA Open Access supplies public-domain images under CC0. Full frame converted to WebP.
assets.requiredAttribution: Jonah Under the Gourd Vine, 280–290 CE. Cleveland Museum of Art, John L. Severance Fund, 1965.239. CC0.
assets.altText: Marble Jonah reclines beneath broad leaves, one arm raised over his head, the other supporting his body; his ankles cross.
assets.historicalFit: Later Christian artistic reception. Costume, posture and plant form cannot establish the appearance of Jonah’s world.
assets.editorialReason: Moves attention from the city to the body sheltered by the plant in the continuation, without answering the book’s final question.
